[[File:Medial hexagonal hexecontahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of a medial hexagonal hexecontahedron]]
In [[geometry]], the '''medial hexagonal hexecontahedron''' (or '''midly dentoid ditriacontahedron''') is a nonconvex [[Isohedral figure|isohedral]] [[polyhedron]]. It is the [[Dual polyhedron|dual]] of the [[uniform star polyhedron|uniform]] [[snub icosidodecadodecahedron]].

==Proportions==

The faces of the medial hexagonal hexecontahedron are irregular nonconvex hexagons. Denote the [[golden ratio]] by <math>\phi</math>, and let <math>\xi\approx -0.377\,438\,833\,12</math> be the real zero of the polynomial <math>8x^3-4x^2+1</math>. The number <math>\xi</math> can be written as <math>\xi=-1/(2\rho)</math>, where <math>\rho</math> is the [[plastic ratio]]. Then each face has four equal angles of <math>\arccos(\xi)\approx 112.175\,128\,045\,27^{\circ}</math>, one of <math>\arccos(\phi^2\xi+\phi)\approx 50.958\,265\,917\,31^{\circ}</math> and one of <math>360^{\circ}-\arccos(\phi^{-2}\xi-\phi^{-1})\approx 220.341\,221\,901\,59^{\circ}</math>. Each face has two long edges, two of medium length and two short ones. If the medium edges have length <math>2</math>, the long ones have length <math>1+\sqrt{(1-\xi)/(-\phi^{-3}-\xi)}\approx 4.121\,448\,816\,41</math> and the short ones <math>1-\sqrt{(1-\xi)/(\phi^{3}-\xi)}\approx 0.453\,587\,559\,98</math>. The [[dihedral angle]] equals <math>\arccos(\xi/(\xi+1))\approx 127.320\,132\,197\,62^{\circ}</math>.
